segments.title: Yokosuka Peace Park, Mikasa, and ships in the harbour
segments.summary: From Yokosuka Peace Park, the group looks over the city museum and waterfront, tentatively picks out Mikasa's mast, and comments on Australian warships in port.
segments.body: Yokosuka Peace Park sits above the Yokosuka City Museum and looks over the surrounding waterfront. The museum is much larger than its modest name suggests, with three official floors and several mezzanines. From the park, the group identifies the offshore island and tentatively picks out Mikasa's mast, then uses those landmarks to work out the location of their hotel. A distant, blocky silhouette prompts a joking debate over whether it is a vehicle carrier or HMAS Canberra, while a Hobart-class destroyer is said to be in dock. The transcript does not settle the distant vessel's identity without the image. The view shows how the museum and Mikasa sit within Yokosuka's active naval waterfront.

evidence.note: They introduce Peace Park, describe the Yokosuka City Museum, orient themselves to Mikasa and the waterfront, debate a distant ship's identity, and mention a Hobart-class destroyer in dock.
